title: Two Communities, One Problem: Branch-and-Bound vs. A* for Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling
abstract: arXiv:2611.14426v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Branch-and-Bound (B&B) and $A^*$ are popular exact search methods originating from Operations Research and Artificial Intelligence, respectively. Although the two methods share fundamental search principles, their different ways of exploring the search space can lead to substantially different computational performance. We investigate these differences using the Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (RCPSP) as an exemplary problem setting. We first establish the relationships between mixed-integer linear programming, state-action, and timed Petri-net representations. Since B&B and $A^*$ admit numerous algorithmic enhancements, we focus on relatively basic implementations. This allows us to examine the fundamental differences between the methods rather than compare the performance of state-of-the-art solvers. translated_title: 两个社区，同一个问题：分支定界法与A*算法在资源受限项目调度中的对比
translated_abstract: 分支定界法和A*分别是源于运筹学和人工智能领域的两种流行的精确搜索方法。尽管这两种方法共享基本的搜索原理，但它们探索搜索空间的不同方式可能导致显著不同的计算性能。我们以资源受限项目调度问题（RCPSP）作为示例问题来研究这些差异。我们首先建立了混合整数线性规划、状态-动作以及时间Petri网表示之间的关系。由于分支定界法和A*算法可以通过众多算法增强手段加以改进，我们聚焦于相对基础的实现方式。这使我们能够考察两种方法之间的根本性差异，而不是比较最先进求解器的性能。通过使用相同的下界和最佳优先节点选择策略，我们隔离了搜索机制本身的影响，特别是……
tldr: 本文以资源受限项目调度问题（RCPSP）为基准，在相同的下界和节点选择策略下，系统比较了运筹学的分支定界法与人工智能的A*搜索算法，并建立了混合整数线性规划、状态-动作和时间Petri网表示之间的联系，从而揭示两种搜索范式的根本性性能差异。
en_tdlr: This paper benchmarks Branch-and-Bound (Operations Research) against A* (Artificial Intelligence) on the Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem, establishing links between mixed-integer linear programming, state-action, and timed Petri-net representations, and isolating the fundamental performance differences between the two search paradigms under identical lower bounds and node selection rules.
